subject: Seller-guided private offer and co-sell approval for Acme AI
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 09:13:00 -0800
Subject: Seller-guided private offer — pricing options + buyer approval checklist

Hi Samantha,

Thanks again for the productive call earlier. Per our conversation, I put together a seller-guided private offer path so Acme AI can get the best unit economics while preserving predictable support and co-sell eligibility with AWS. Attached are two artifacts to review: a short price schedule (RDW_AWS_PrivateOffer_Pricing_v1.pdf) and our internal co-sell playbook extract (CoSell_Playbook_v2.docx).

High-level ask for you so we can draft the private offer in AWS and route approvals:
- Confirm the AWS payer account ID where the private offer should be delivered.
- Confirm buyer-side approvers (Finance, Legal, IT) and their expected approval SLAs.
- Preferred term: 12, 24, or 36 months? (We recommend 36 months for max discount but can do a 12-month with smaller discount.)
- Expected committed monthly spend (ballpark) so we can size the SKU quantities.

Pricing options we recommend (summary):
- 12 months: list price with 10% volume discount on committed spend
- 24 months: 18% committed discount + invoicing options (monthly or quarterly)
- 36 months: 25% committed discount with an optional 30% upfront payment term for additional credits

Buyer approval notes (seller-guided flow):
1) We create the private offer in AWS Marketplace and share the Offer ID with your procurement team.
2) Procurement/Finance logs into your AWS account (needs Marketplace admin role) and accepts the private offer.
3) Your procurement team issues a PO referencing the private offer ID to complete onboarding; AWS will surface billing per the private offer cadence.

If you can reply with the account ID, procurement contact, and preferred term, we’ll generate the Seller Private Offer (SPO) draft and loop in our AWS PDM (Diego) to support acceptance and co-sell tagging.

Next step suggestion: if you want, I can draft the SPO for the 36-month option and we can iterate.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0138
Redwood Inference

Samantha —

Great, thanks for the quick context and the payer account ID. I’m looping in Vanessa and Marissa to coordinate legal/finance artifacts and also Diego from AWS so we have the PDM in the loop for co-sell tagging and acceptance assistance.

A few clarifications and next steps from Redwood:
- PO vs DocuSign: Redwood can accept a Buyer PO that references the AWS Private Offer ID as sufficient to enable billing. If Procurement requires a countersigned DocuSign, we can provide that as an optional step; it won't be required to create the private offer in AWS.
- Term + opt-out: We can do a 36-month commitment with a 12–18 month reasonable exit clause for under-usage (we suggest an early-termination fee schedule rather than an absolute opt-out — we’ll put language in the SOW).
- Billing cadence: monthly billing by default (invoiced through AWS Marketplace). For upfront credit we can provide additional discounts (we included the 30% upfront option in the attached pricing).

Proposed next step timeline:
1) Redwood: prepare SPO draft for 36-month committed option and a parallel 12-month baseline (to keep Legal options open). Target: shared by EOD tomorrow.
2) Acme Procurement: confirm PO template and whether you want the DocuSign copy attached for Legal.
3) AWS PDM (Diego): once SPO is created, assist Acme in locating and accepting the offer in the AWS console and ensure co-sell flagging.

I will attach a PO template and a short Legal note for your counsel in the next message (Marissa is drafting it now).

Jordan

Hi all —

Quick operational notes from AWS side to smooth acceptance:
- The buyer must be signed into the AWS account that will be billed (payer account). If Acme is using an AWS Organization, Procurement should accept the private offer from the master payer console.
- Private Offer visibility: once you create the SPO and mark it as "Private", it will appear in the buyer's console under "Private offers to your account" and also optionally in the Billing -> Marketplace tab.
- Acceptance window: the private offer link we share will be active for 14 calendar days by default. If you need more time for Legal, we can request an extension when creating the offer.
- Multi-year billing: this is supported via Marketplace as a committed spend schedule; AWS will surface invoices per the billing cadence (monthly if selected). Make sure the buyer PO references the private offer ID (that is the key artifact).
- Co-sell: to ensure the deal is eligible for co-sell incentives, please confirm the AWS AE/PDM who owns the account and request tagging when the offer is accepted. I will coordinate with Partner Central after acceptance.

If helpful, I can do a quick 20-minute walkthrough with Procurement on where to accept the SPO in their console.

Diego Ramirez
